name: Chicken Lo Mein Noodle Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 6.25 lb (2800 g)
Egg Noodles (Great Value wide): 31.5 oz dry (892 g)
Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 4.5 oz (126 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Whisk the sauce: hoisin, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil, chicken broth, and cornstarch in a bowl until smooth. Set it by the stove.
Boil the egg noodles 1 minute short of the package time, drain, and toss with a little oil so they do not clump.
Slice the chicken breast into thin strips. Working in batches, sear in vegetable oil over high heat until cooked through to 165 F. Set aside.
In the same pot, stir fry the sliced red bell pepper 2 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, and most of the green onions for 1 minute more.
Return the chicken, pour in the sauce, and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until it thickens and turns glossy.
Add the noodles and toss until every strand is coated. Finish with the remaining green onions.
Portion into 14 containers while still warm so the sauce distributes evenly.
head_steps: Whisk hoisin, soy, oyster sauce, sesame oil, broth, and cornstarch into a sauce.
Boil egg noodles just short of done and toss with a little oil.
Sear sliced chicken to 165 F, then stir fry pepper, garlic, ginger, and green onions.
Return chicken, add sauce, and simmer until glossy.
Toss in the noodles, coat well, and portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: Salt (1 tbsp) and black pepper (0.5 tbsp) are costed but no step salts the noodle water, seasons the chicken, or says 'season'.

name: Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 4.75 lb (2183 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken breast into large pieces, season it with the cajun seasoning, and brown it in the vegetable oil in a heavy pot. Set it aside.

Melt the butter in the same pot, whisk in the flour, and now settle in. Stir constantly over medium-low heat for 25 to 30 minutes until the roux turns the color of milk chocolate. Do not answer the phone. If black flecks appear, throw it out and start over, because a burnt roux poisons the entire pot.
Add the diced onion, bell pepper, and celery straight into the hot roux. It will hiss and stop the cooking, which is exactly what you want. Cook 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, thyme, smoked paprika, italian seasoning, bay leaves, salt, and pepper and stir for a minute.
Pour in the chicken broth slowly while whisking so the roux incorporates smoothly instead of clumping, then return the chicken.
Simmer uncovered for 45 minutes, skimming any fat that rises. The gumbo should thicken to the point where it coats a spoon but still pours.
Cook the rice, then stir the sliced green onions in off the heat.
head_steps: Season and brown the chicken pieces, then set aside.
Whisk flour into melted butter and stir constantly 25 to 30 minutes until the roux is milk chocolate colored.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and celery to the roux and cook 8 minutes, then add garlic and seasonings.
Whisk in the chicken broth slowly, return the chicken, and simmer uncovered 45 minutes.
Cook the rice, stir in green onions, and portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: 1.25 lb of sausage is costed and the dish is titled 'Chicken and Sausage Gumbo', but no step ever browns or adds the sausage; the source (africanbites.com) browns it in step 2 and returns it near the end.
Step 5 adds 'garlic, thyme, smoked paprika, italian seasoning, bay leaves, salt, and pepper' but italian seasoning is not in the costed list (and is not in the source either).

name: Coq au Vin
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 6.25 lb (2800 g)
Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 0.25 lb (126 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the chopped bacon in a heavy pot until crisp, then lift it out and leave the fat behind.
Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper and brown them hard in the bacon fat in batches. This is the color of the finished dish, so take it further than feels comfortable.
Add the quartered onions and carrots and cook until they take on color, then add the garlic and tomato paste and cook another minute.
Pour in the beef broth and chicken broth, scraping every brown bit off the bottom, and add the thyme and bay leaves. Return the chicken and the bacon.
Cover and simmer low for about 45 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the vegetables are soft.
Brown the mushrooms separately in butter over high heat and add them at the end. Mushrooms thrown in at the start turn gray and rubbery, and browning them apart is what keeps them worth eating.
Knead the rest of the butter with flour into a paste and stir it into the simmering pot a little at a time until the sauce coats a spoon. Cook the rice and serve the braise over it.
head_steps: Crisp the chopped bacon and remove it, leaving the fat.
Brown the seasoned chicken thighs hard in the bacon fat, then set aside.
Color the onions and carrots, add garlic and tomato paste, then deglaze with both broths.
Return the chicken and bacon with thyme and bay leaves and simmer covered 45 minutes.
Brown the mushrooms separately in butter and add at the end.
Thicken with butter kneaded into flour, then portion over rice into 14 containers.

findings.detail: Step 5 says to 'add the thyme and bay leaves' but bay leaves are not in our costed ingredient list.
Step 8 says to 'knead the rest of the butter with flour into a paste' (the source's beurre manie thickener) but flour is not in our costed ingredient list.

name: Country Pork Meatballs with Onion Gravy over Mashed Potatoes
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 400F and line two sheet pans. Put a pot of salted water on for the potatoes.

In a big bowl combine the ground pork, bread crumbs, eggs, green onions, garlic, italian seasoning, onion powder, paprika, dried thyme, salt and black pepper. Mix with your hands only until it comes together, because overworking it makes the meatballs tough.
Roll even meatballs, space them out on the sheet pans, and bake until browned and cooked through.
Peel and chunk the potatoes, boil until a fork slides in easy, then drain and mash with a little of the butter, salt and pepper.
Melt the rest of the butter in a wide pot and cook the sliced yellow onion low and slow until it turns deep golden and sweet. That patience is the whole flavor of the gravy.
Sprinkle the flour over the onions and stir for a minute, then pour in the beef broth along with the worcestershire and soy sauce. Whisk until it thickens into a glossy gravy.
Slide the baked meatballs into the gravy and let them simmer a few minutes so they drink some of it up.
head_steps: Mix the ground pork with bread crumbs, eggs, green onions, garlic and seasonings, then roll into meatballs.
Bake the meatballs on lined sheet pans at 400F until browned and cooked through.
Boil the potatoes until tender and mash with butter, salt and pepper.
Cook the sliced onions in butter until deep golden, stir in flour, then whisk in beef broth, Worcestershire and soy sauce until thickened.
Simmer the meatballs in the gravy, then serve over the mashed potatoes.

findings.detail: We buy 5.25 tbsp (71 g) olive oil but our steps bake the meatballs on sheet pans and build the gravy entirely on butter; the source (RecipeTin) uses its 1.5 tbsp oil to pan-brown the meatballs, a step our adaptation removed without removing the purchase.

name: Creamy Ground Turkey Shell Pasta
ingredients: Pasta Shells (Great Value): 28 oz dry (794 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the pasta shells 1 minute short of package time, drain, and set aside.
Brown the ground turkey in half the olive oil in your big pot, breaking it up until no pink remains. Season with salt, pepper, and the Italian seasoning. Set aside.
Add the remaining oil and saute the sliced mushrooms, diced onion, and diced bell pepper until the mushrooms release their water and brown, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir 1 to 2 minutes to cook it out.
Slowly whisk in the beef broth, then the heavy cream. Simmer 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Return the turkey, stir in the parmesan, and fold in the shells until coated.
Portion into 14 containers while the sauce is still loose.
head_steps: Boil shells just short of done and drain.
Brown seasoned ground turkey and set aside.
Saute mushrooms, onion, and pepper, add garlic, then cook in the flour.
Whisk in beef broth and cream and simmer until thick, then return turkey with parmesan.
Fold in the shells and portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: We buy 2.3 cans (992 g) of tomato sauce but our sauce step only whisks in beef broth then heavy cream; the source (Kroll's Korner step 4) pours in 'beef broth and tomato sauce' together, so our steps silently dropped a core sauce component the shopper paid for.

name: Creamy Turkey and Rice Soup with Mushrooms
ingredients: Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 0.5 lb (265 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the wild rice separately per the package until tender and set it aside. It takes longer than white rice, so start it first.
Chop the bacon and render it in your big pot with the olive oil until crisp, then lift the bacon out and leave the fat behind.
Add the butter, then the diced onion, celery and carrots, and cook until soft. Add the sliced mushrooms and cook until they give up their water and start to brown.
Stir in the garlic, the dried thyme and the Italian seasoning, then sprinkle the flour over everything and stir for two minutes to cook out the raw taste.
Pour in the chicken broth slowly while stirring so the roux does not lump, then simmer until it thickens.
Add the cooked wild rice, the turkey breast and the heavy cream, warm it through without boiling, then finish with the lemon juice, the reserved bacon, salt and black pepper.
head_steps: Cook the wild rice separately until tender and set aside.
Render the bacon in the pot, remove it, and cook the onion, celery, carrots and mushrooms in the fat and butter.
Stir in the garlic and herbs, dust with flour, and cook two minutes.
Whisk in the chicken broth and simmer until thickened.
Add the wild rice, turkey breast and cream, warm through, and finish with lemon juice and the bacon.

findings.detail: Steps say 'Cook the wild rice separately... It takes longer than white rice, so start it first' and later 'Add the cooked wild rice', but the list buys plain Rice (Member's Mark) white rice; the wild-rice language survived the budget swap from the source's wild-rice soup.

name: Curry Ground Turkey Bowls
steps: Brown the ground turkey in a large skillet, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the chopped onion and cook until soft, then stir in the chili powder and cumin.
Pour in the diced tomatoes and coconut milk and stir it all together.
Simmer 10 to 15 minutes until the sauce thickens and turns rich.
Serve the curry over cooked white rice.
head_steps: Brown the ground turkey in a large skillet, breaking it up as it cooks.
Add the chopped onion and cook until soft, then stir in the chili powder and cumin.
Pour in the diced tomatoes and coconut milk and stir it all together.
Simmer 10 to 15 minutes until the sauce thickens and turns rich.
Serve the curry over cooked white rice.

findings.detail: The dish is named Curry Ground Turkey Bowls and we buy curry powder, but the steps only add 'the chili powder and cumin'; the source (Family Food on the Table step 3) blooms curry powder as the lead spice.
We buy 1 cup frozen peas (490 g) but no step ever adds them; the source is literally titled 'Curry Ground Turkey with Rice and Peas' and stirs the peas in with the tomatoes.
We buy 2 cloves minced garlic but the steps go straight from onion to spices; the source sautes garlic with the onion in step 1.
We buy 1 tsp EVOO but step 1 just says 'Brown the ground turkey in a large skillet' with no oil mention anywhere.
Salt is in the costed list but no step says salt or 'season'; this card's steps are an outlier (5 steps, no weigh-the-pot opener) and look truncated versus the rest of the catalog.

name: Dak Galbi (Korean Chicken and Cabbage Skillet)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 5.25 lb (2333 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 4.75 tbsp (25 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the rice cakes in warm water for 20 minutes if they came refrigerated or frozen, so they soften evenly instead of staying hard in the center.
Whisk the gochujang, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, ginger, curry powder, red pepper flakes, and black pepper with the chicken broth into a marinade.
Cut the chicken breast into bite sized pieces and toss with about half the marinade. Let it sit 20 minutes.

Cut the cabbage into wide ribbons, the sweet potato and carrot into thin slices, and the onion into wedges. Thin slices matter for the sweet potato, because it cooks slower than everything else in the pan.
Heat the vegetable oil in your largest skillet over high heat and cook the chicken until it browns at the edges, working in batches so the pan stays hot.
Add the sweet potato, carrot, onion, and drained rice cakes with the rest of the marinade and cook 8 minutes, stirring, until the rice cakes soften.
Fold in the cabbage last and cook 5 more minutes, just until it wilts but still has bite. Overcooked cabbage turns watery and takes the sauce with it.
head_steps: Soak the rice cakes in warm water until pliable.
Whisk gochujang, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, ginger, curry powder, and pepper flakes with broth into a marinade.
Toss the cut chicken with half the marinade and rest 20 minutes.
Brown the chicken in batches in a hot skillet.
Add sweet potato, carrot, onion, rice cakes, and the rest of the marinade and cook 8 minutes.
Fold in the cabbage for 5 minutes, then weigh and divide into 14 containers.

findings.detail: We buy 1 tbsp (20 g) salt but the marinade step enumerates every other seasoning (gochujang, soy, sugar, garlic, ginger, curry powder, red pepper flakes, black pepper) and no step says salt or 'season'.

name: Ethiopian Doro Wat Chicken Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7 lb (3175 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken thighs into large chunks and toss with the lemon juice and a big pinch of salt. Let them sit while you cook the onions.

Finely chop the red onions and cook them dry in your big pot over medium-low heat, stirring often, 15 to 20 minutes until soft and deeply golden. This slow onion melt is the backbone of doro wat, so do not rush it.
Add the vegetable oil, garlic, and ginger and cook 2 minutes. Stir in the berbere and paprika and toast 1 to 2 minutes until brick red and fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the chicken broth. Simmer 10 minutes to marry the sauce.
Add the chicken and simmer gently, partially covered, 25 to 30 minutes until it reaches 165 F and the sauce has thickened. Stir in the butter at the end for gloss.
Meanwhile, hard boil the eggs: 11 minutes in boiling water, then an ice bath, then peel. Prick or slash each egg lightly and let them warm in the sauce for the last 5 minutes.
Portion into 14 containers with a hard boiled egg or so in each, covered in sauce.
head_steps: Toss chunked chicken thighs with lemon juice and salt.
Slow-cook chopped red onions until deeply golden, then add garlic, ginger, and toasted berbere.
Stir in tomato paste and broth and simmer the sauce.
Braise the chicken to 165 F until the sauce thickens; finish with butter.
Add peeled hard boiled eggs and portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: We buy 0.5 tbsp black pepper but the only seasoning in our steps is 'a big pinch of salt' in step 2 and no step says 'season'; the source (Chili Pepper Madness) seasons with salt and pepper in its flavor-base and chicken steps.

name: Filipino Beef Caldereta
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 5.5 oz (159 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the potatoes and carrots into big chunks and fry them in the vegetable oil until browned on the outside, then set them aside. This keeps them from disintegrating during the braise.
Season the cubed beef with salt and pepper and brown it hard in the same pot in batches.
Cook the onion and garlic until soft, then add the tomato sauce, tomato paste, soy sauce, and the broths and scrape the bottom of the pot clean.
Return the beef, bring it to a simmer, cover, and cook low for about 2 hours until it is fork tender.
Blend the chicken livers with a ladle of the hot broth until smooth and stir the mixture back into the pot along with the peanut butter. Let it simmer 10 minutes to thicken.
Add the fried potatoes and carrots, the sliced red and green peppers, and the olives and cook another 20 minutes, until the vegetables are tender and the sauce coats a spoon.
Stir the shredded cheddar in off the heat until it melts into the sauce, then taste for salt.
head_steps: Fry the potato and carrot chunks until browned, then set aside.
Brown the seasoned beef in batches, then cook the onion and garlic.
Add tomato sauce, tomato paste, soy sauce, and broth, return the beef, and simmer covered about 2 hours.
Blend the chicken livers with hot broth and stir in with the peanut butter to thicken.
Add the fried vegetables, peppers, and olives and simmer 20 minutes, then melt in the cheddar.
Weigh the pot and divide into 14 containers.

findings.detail: Step 4 says to add 'the tomato sauce, tomato paste, soy sauce, and the broths' and step 6 blends livers 'with a ladle of the hot broth', but no broth of any kind is in the costed list (the source uses water plus beef powder).

name: Filipino Beef Pares Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck roast into large cubes. Sear them hard in a little oil, in batches, until they have real color on at least two sides.
Add chopped onion, half the garlic, and the ginger to the pot and cook until the onion goes soft and translucent.
Pour in the chicken broth, soy sauce, and brown sugar. Add bay leaves and black pepper, scraping the browned bits off the bottom.
Cover and simmer low for 2 to 2.5 hours, until the beef pulls apart with a spoon. Add water if the pot gets too dry.
Uncover for the last 20 minutes and let the sauce reduce until it coats the beef instead of pooling around it.
For the garlic rice, fry the remaining sliced garlic in the rest of the oil until golden, then toss in the cooked cold rice and stir until every grain is coated and hot.
Finish with sliced green onions over the beef.
head_steps: Sear cubed chuck roast in batches until well browned.
Cook onion, garlic, and ginger in the same pot until soft.
Add broth, soy sauce, and brown sugar and simmer covered 2 to 2.5 hours.
Uncover and reduce the sauce until it coats the beef.
Fry sliced garlic in oil, toss with cold cooked rice, and portion into 14 containers.

findings.detail: We buy a substantial 3.5 tbsp (63 g) of salt but no step uses it and none says 'season'; the source salts its broth with 1 tbsp and seasons the asado and rice to taste.

name: Filipino Pork Menudo Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the pork shoulder into cubes and season with salt and black pepper.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot, stir in the achiote paste until it colors the oil, then brown the pork in batches.
Add the diced yellow onion and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in the diced tomatoes and fish sauce, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook until the pork is starting to turn tender.
Add the cubed potatoes, carrots, and chicken livers and simmer uncovered until the vegetables are cooked through and the sauce reduces.
Fold in the chickpeas, diced green and red bell peppers, and golden raisins, and cook just until the peppers soften but keep some bite.
Taste and adjust the salt, then cook rice separately to serve underneath.
head_steps: Cube and season the pork, then brown it in achiote-colored oil.
Cook the onion and garlic until soft.
Add diced tomatoes and fish sauce and simmer covered until the pork softens.
Add potatoes, carrots, and chicken livers and simmer until tender.
Fold in chickpeas, bell peppers, and raisins and cook briefly.
Cook rice separately and portion the stew over it into 14 containers.

findings.detail: The dish is 'Pork Menudo Rice Bowls' and the final step says 'cook rice separately to serve underneath', but rice is not in the costed list, unlike every sibling rice-bowl card in this chunk.

name: Five Spice Turkey Noodle Bowls
ingredients: Lo Mein Noodles (Simply Asia): 45.5 oz dry (1293 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the mushrooms thick. Thin slices vanish into a broth like this, and you want them to stay recognizable in the bowl.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot, add the ground turkey, and brown it hard, breaking it into crumbles, until it is cooked through to 165F.
Add the mushrooms and cook 6 minutes without stirring much, so they release their water and then start to brown instead of steam.
Add the minced garlic and the five spice powder and stir for one minute. This blooming step wakes the spice up, and it is the whole reason this bowl tastes like more than salty broth.
Pour in the chicken broth, season with salt and black pepper, and simmer 15 minutes so the flavors marry.
Stir in the hot honey off the heat and taste. It should read savory first and sweet second.
Boil the lo mein noodles just short of done, drain them, rinse them cold so they stop cooking, and move them into your weighed pot.
head_steps: Slice the mushrooms thick.
Brown the ground turkey in olive oil to 165F.
Add the mushrooms and cook 6 minutes until browned.
Add garlic and five spice powder and bloom one minute, then add the chicken broth and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in the hot honey off the heat.
Cook and rinse the noodles, portion by weight into 14 containers, and ladle the broth over the top.

findings.detail: We buy 14.75 tbsp (88 g) of green onions but no step slices or adds them; the source (Jennie-O step 6) garnishes the finished bowls with the green onions.

name: Frito Pie Walking Taco Casserole
ingredients: Diced Tomatoes & Green Chilies (Great Value (Ro-Tel style)): 2.3 cans (662 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 9.25 oz (264 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the olive oil in a big pot and cook the diced onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the ground beef and break it up as it browns. Cook until no pink remains, then stir in the taco seasoning and salt.
Add the drained kidney beans, the diced tomatoes with green chilies with their juice, and the tomato sauce. Simmer 10 minutes so it thickens into a proper chili.
Spread the chili into a baking dish, top with the Mexican cheese blend, and bake at 350F until the cheese is melted and bubbly, about 15 minutes.
Portion the chili into 14 containers. Keep the corn chips in the bag; add a handful on top after reheating so they stay crunchy instead of turning to mush.
head_steps: Cook onion and garlic in olive oil, then brown the ground beef and stir in taco seasoning.
Add drained kidney beans, diced tomatoes with green chilies, and tomato sauce; simmer 10 minutes.
Spread into a baking dish, top with cheese, and bake at 350F until melted and bubbly.
Portion into 14 containers; add corn chips on top after reheating so they stay crunchy.

findings.detail: We buy 0.5 tbsp black pepper but the steps season only with taco seasoning and salt and no step says 'season'; the source list has no black pepper either, so ours is a purchase with no use anywhere.

name: Greek Beef and Chickpea Bowls
ingredients: Feta Cheese (Great Value crumbled): 7 oz (200 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice: rinse it, then simmer covered with water until tender and set it aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet, add the ground beef, and break it up as it browns. Cook until no pink remains.
Season the beef with the garlic powder, dried oregano, dried dill, salt, and black pepper, and let it toast in the spices for 2 minutes.
While the beef cooks, dice the cucumber, halve the cherry tomatoes, and slice the red onion thin.
Build each container: rice on the bottom, seasoned beef, a scoop of hummus, a scoop of Greek yogurt, then cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, and crumbled feta.
Portion evenly across 14 containers. Keep the yogurt and hummus to one side of the box if you plan to reheat, then stir them in after.
head_steps: Cook the rice and set it aside.
Brown the ground beef in olive oil, then season with garlic powder, oregano, dill, salt, and pepper.
Dice the cucumber, halve the cherry tomatoes, and slice the red onion.
Layer rice, beef, hummus, Greek yogurt, fresh vegetables, and feta into 14 containers.

findings.detail: Chickpeas are in the dish's name and we buy 5.8 cans (1488 g), yet no step drains, heats, or plates them; the source (Chelsea's Messy Apron step 1) folds the chickpeas into the browning beef.

name: Greek Ground Turkey Lemon Rice Bowls
ingredients: Feta Cheese (Great Value crumbled): 7 oz (200 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat a splash of the olive oil in your biggest pot and cook the diced onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the ground turkey and break it up as it browns. Cook until it reaches 165F and no pink remains. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in the rinsed rice, chicken broth, lemon juice, and enough water to cook the rice. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook 15 to 18 minutes until the rice is tender.
Stir in the rest of the olive oil and the sliced olives, then taste for salt. Lemon rice should make your mouth water a little.
Portion into 14 containers and top each with crumbled feta.
head_steps: Cook onion and garlic in olive oil, then brown the ground turkey to 165F.
Add rice, chicken broth, lemon juice, and water; cover and simmer until the rice is tender.
Stir in the remaining olive oil and sliced olives, then season.
Portion into 14 containers and top with crumbled feta.

findings.detail: We buy 17.25 tbsp (60 g) of sun-dried tomatoes but step 5 stirs in only the olive oil and olives; the source (Chelsea's Messy Apron) stirs sun-dried tomatoes in with the olives and lemon off the heat.

name: Greek Turkey Moussaka
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Slice the eggplant into rounds, salt them, and let them sit 20 minutes to draw out water. Pat them dry, brush them with the olive oil, and roast at 425F for about 25 minutes until they are soft and browned.
While the eggplant roasts, cook the diced onion in a large pot until soft, add the garlic for a minute, then brown the ground turkey until it reaches 165F.

Add the tomato sauce, beef broth, cinnamon, oregano, red wine vinegar, bay leaves, salt, and pepper. Simmer 20 minutes until the sauce is thick and almost dry, because a wet meat layer means a soggy casserole.

Make the bechamel: melt the butter, whisk in the flour and cook two minutes, then pour in the milk slowly while whisking until it thickens. Off the heat, whisk in the beaten eggs, the parmesan, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Layer the roasted eggplant and the meat sauce in your baking pans, pour the bechamel over the top, and smooth it flat.
Bake at 350F for 45 minutes until the top is set and golden, then let it rest at least 20 minutes so the squares hold together when you cut them.
Cook the rice, move it into your weighed pot, and cut the moussaka into 14 even squares.
head_steps: Salt and drain the sliced eggplant, brush with olive oil, and roast at 425F for 25 minutes.
Cook onion and garlic, brown the ground turkey to 165F, then add tomato sauce, broth, cinnamon, oregano, vinegar, and bay leaves and simmer 20 minutes until thick.
Whisk a bechamel from butter, flour, and milk, then finish off heat with eggs, parmesan, and nutmeg.
Layer eggplant and meat sauce in pans and top with bechamel.
Bake at 350F for 45 minutes and rest 20 minutes.
Cook the rice, portion it by weight into 14 containers, and set one moussaka square on each.

findings.detail: We buy 15.3 potatoes (3268 g), the second-largest line on the card, but the steps layer only eggplant, meat sauce, and bechamel and never boil, slice, or layer a potato; the source (Coley Cooks) states a true moussaka 'will only have eggplant and meat topped with a white sauce'.
The final step says 'Cook the rice, move it into your weighed pot, and cut the moussaka into 14 even squares', but rice is not in the costed list (and the source serves moussaka with no rice at all).

name: Greek Turkey Youvarlakia (Egg-Lemon Meatball and Rice)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Mix the ground turkey with the uncooked rice, grated onion, the dried dill, salt, and black pepper. The rice goes in raw and cooks inside the meatball, which is the whole idea.
Roll the mixture into meatballs and set them aside. Do not pack them tight, since the rice needs room to swell.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pot, soften the remaining diced onion and the grated carrot for 6 minutes, then add water to make a light broth and bring it to a simmer.
Lower the meatballs in gently, cover, and simmer 40 minutes until the rice inside is tender and the meat is cooked through to 165F. Do not stir hard, just shake the pot.

Make the avgolemono: whisk the eggs until frothy, whisk in the lemon juice, then ladle in hot broth one spoon at a time while whisking constantly. This tempering step is the only part that can go wrong, so go slow.
Pour the sauce back into the pot off the heat and swirl the pot to combine. Never let it boil again, because boiling scrambles the eggs and there is no undo.
Scatter the chopped fresh herb over the top, then move everything into your weighed pot.
head_steps: Mix ground turkey with uncooked rice, grated onion, dried dill, salt, and pepper, then roll into meatballs.
Soften the remaining onion and grated carrot in olive oil and add water to make a light broth.
Simmer the meatballs covered 40 minutes until the rice is tender and the meat reaches 165F.
Whisk eggs with lemon juice, then temper with hot broth one ladle at a time.
Stir the sauce back into the pot off the heat without letting it boil.
Portion by weight into 14 containers, dividing meatballs by count.

findings.detail: Final step says 'Scatter the chopped fresh herb over the top' but the list contains no fresh herb (only dried dill); the source garnishes with fresh parsley, which we never buy.

name: Ground Beef and Broccoli Bowls
ingredients: Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
steps: Brown 4.9 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion, then drain any excess fat.
Steam or microwave the broccoli florets until bright green and just tender.
Whisk the soy sauce, beef broth, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and cornstarch into a quick sauce.
Pour the sauce over the beef and simmer until it thickens and glossy-coats the meat.
Fold in the broccoli, then serve everything over cooked rice in each container.
head_steps: Brown 4.9 pounds of 93/7 ground beef with the chopped onion, then drain any excess fat.

name: Ground Turkey Lasagna Casserole
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 3.75 tbsp (20 g)
Pasta Shells - jumbo (Great Value): 22.25 oz dry (633 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 9.75 oz (278 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the jumbo shells to just under done, about 2 minutes short of the box time, then drain them. They finish in the oven and overcooked pasta in a bake turns to paste.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot, cook the diced onion 5 minutes, add the garlic for a minute, then brown the ground turkey until it is cooked through to 165F.
Add the marinara sauce, the chicken broth, the italian seasoning, red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper, and simmer 10 minutes so it thickens up.
Stir the ricotta together with the eggs and the parmesan in a separate bowl. The egg is what keeps the ricotta from weeping water into your casserole.
Fold the drained shells into the meat sauce, then dollop the ricotta mixture through it and stir just twice so you get ribbons of white instead of a uniform pink.
Spread it in your baking pans, cover with the mozzarella, and bake at 375F for 30 minutes until it bubbles at the edges and the cheese browns in spots.
Let it rest 15 minutes, cook the rice, and move the rice into your weighed pot.
head_steps: Boil the jumbo shells 2 minutes short of done and drain.
Cook onion and garlic in olive oil, then brown the ground turkey to 165F.
Add marinara, chicken broth, and seasonings and simmer 10 minutes.
Mix ricotta with eggs and parmesan, then fold the shells and ricotta into the sauce.
Top with mozzarella and bake at 375F for 30 minutes, then rest 15 minutes.
Cook the rice, portion it by weight into 14 containers, and set a casserole square on each.
